notes.text:
**Genesis 27:19** — קוּם־נָא שְׁבָה וְאׇכְלָה מִצֵּידִי בַּעֲבוּר תְּבָרְכַנִּי נַפְשֶׁךָ. Jacob, dressed as Esau, asks Isaac to sit up and eat "of my game." Rav Tzadok's question: the dish was goat-kids, not game, and "of my game" was needless; he answers at the end of the os ("my hunt" = trapping the lying tongue).
*Mafteach: found*

**Bereshit Rabbah 67:2** (on Genesis 27:33, מִי־אֵפוֹא הוּא הַצָּד־צַיִד) — הוּא הַצָּד צַיִד, אָמַר רַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר בַּר שִׁמְעוֹן צַיָּדָא הֵיךְ צָדוּךְ. "Hunter, how were you hunted?" — Esau the trapper was himself trapped. Rav Tzadok reads this as the key to "מִצֵּידִי": Jacob's "hunt" was the outwitting of the hunter.
*Mafteach: found*

**Micah 7:20** — תִּתֵּן אֱמֶת לְיַעֲקֹב חֶסֶד לְאַבְרָהָם. Truth is Jacob's defining attribute; the whole os asks how that attribute coexists with the stratagem of the blessings.
*Mafteach: found*

**Megillah 13b** — אֲמַר לַהּ: אָחִיו אֲנָא בְּרַמָּאוּת. אֲמַרָה לֵיהּ: וּמִי שְׁרֵי לְצַדִּיקֵי לְסַגּוֹיֵי בְּרַמָּיוּתָא? אֲמַר לַהּ, אִין: ״עִם נָבָר תִּתָּבָר וְעִם עִקֵּשׁ תִּתַּפָּל״. Jacob tells Rachel he is Laban's "brother in trickery"; asked whether the righteous may act with guile, he answers with the verse. The same exchange is in Bava Batra 123a.
*Mafteach: found*

**II Samuel 22:27** — עִם־נָבָר תִּתָּבָר וְעִם־עִקֵּשׁ תִּתַּפָּל (parallel Psalms 18:27 reads תִּתְפַּתָּל). "With the crooked You deal subtly": the verse Jacob cites in Megillah 13b, which Rav Tzadok makes the rule for answering a deceiver.
*Mafteach: found*

**Genesis 27:35** — וַיֹּאמֶר בָּא אָחִיךָ בְּמִרְמָה וַיִּקַּח בִּרְכָתֶךָ. Isaac to Esau: "Your brother came with guile and took your blessing."
*Mafteach: missing*

**Targum Onkelos, Genesis 27:35** — וַאֲמַר עַל אָחוּךְ בְּחָכְמְתָא וְקַבִּיל בִּרְכְּתָךְ. Onkelos renders מִרְמָה as "wisdom" (printed editions: בְּחָכְמְתָא).
*Mafteach: missing*

**Bereshit Rabbah 67:4** — בָּא אָחִיךָ בְּמִרְמָה, רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן אָמַר בָּא בְּחָכְמַת תּוֹרָתוֹ. R. Yochanan: Jacob came "with the wisdom of his Torah." Rav Tzadok joins Onkelos and the Midrash: the guile was Torah-wisdom.
*Mafteach: missing*

**Parallels beyond the library:**
**Degel Machaneh Ephraim, Addenda on Torah, Toldot 3** (Chassidus) — the same problem (how could Jacob, a man of truth, say "אנכי עשו"?) and the same sources, Onkelos בחכמה and the Midrash's בחכמת תורתו: Jacob is the chariot of the Vav, which is Torah, and his "אנכי" is the Torah's "Anochi."
ולכאורה יעקב איש אמת ידבר שקר חלילה

**Proverbs 8:12** — אֲנִי־חׇכְמָה שָׁכַנְתִּי עׇרְמָה וְדַעַת מְזִמּוֹת אֶמְצָא. "I, Wisdom, dwell with shrewdness": shrewdness is housed inside wisdom, not opposed to it.
*Mafteach: found*

**Parallels:**
**Tzidkat HaTzadik 219** (Rav Tzadok) — the same verse, with Sotah 21b (נִכְנְסָה חָכְמָה – נִכְנְסָה עַרְמוּמִיּוּת): wherever wisdom enters, cunning enters with it. There it is the danger of growing wisdom; here Rav Tzadok turns the pairing toward holiness, as the shrewdness Torah teaches for meeting a deceiver. *checked*

**Zohar I 145b** (Zohar, Toldot 19:185) — אֲנִי חָכְמָה, דָּא כְּנֶסֶת יִשְׂרָאֵל. שָׁכַנְתִּי עָרְמָה, דָּא יַעֲקֹב דְּאִיהוּ חַכִּים, וְדַעַת מְזִמּוֹת אֶמְצָא דָּא יִצְחָק. R. Chiyya reads the verse on the blessings: Wisdom is Knesses Yisrael, "shrewdness" is Jacob the wise, and "knowledge of designs" is Isaac who intended to bless Esau.
*Mafteach: found*

**Parallels beyond the library:**
**Ketem Paz on Zohar 145a:14** (Kabbalah) — on the Zohar Rav Tzadok cites: "shrewdness" is Jacob because his attribute draws from both Chesed and Pachad, and the left side is shrewdness; wisdom joining Jacob is what brought the blessings.
שכנתי ערמה דא יעקב כי מדתו של יעקב יונק מהחס"ד וגם מהפחד שהוא הערמה

**Avodah Zarah 4b** — תּוֹרָה דִּכְתִיב בַּהּ ״אֱמֶת״, דִּכְתִיב: ״אֱמֶת קְנֵה וְאַל תִּמְכֹּר״ (Proverbs 23:23). Torah is the realm called "truth." Rav Tzadok's step: the wisdom that houses shrewdness is Torah, which is itself truth, so the shrewdness learned from it is an expression of truth.
*Mafteach: found*

**Zohar I 138a** (Zohar, Toldot 4:26) — בְּגִין דְּאִתְמְשַׁךְ עֵשָׂו אֲבַתְרִיהּ דְּהַהוּא נָחָשׁ, אָזִיל עִמֵּיהּ יַעֲקֹב בְּעֲקִימָא, כְּנָחָשׁ דְּאִיהוּ חַכִּים... בְּגִין לְאַמְשָׁכָא לֵיהּ לְעֵשָׂו בַּתְרֵיהּ דְּהַהוּא נָחָשׁ, וְיִתְפְּרַשׁ מִנֵּיהּ. Because Esau followed the serpent, Jacob dealt with him crookedly, as the serpent does, to draw Esau wholly after it and so be separated from him, leaving him no share in this world or the next.
*Mafteach: found*

**Parallels beyond the library:**
**Ohr HaChammah on Zohar 1:138a:6** (Kabbalah) — R. Chaim Vital on the same Zohar asks how the "ish tam" could act with guile toward Esau and Laban, answers with עם עקש תתפל and the rider-of-the-serpent passage (Zohar I 137b), and adds that the serpent strives to cling to holiness, so one must go its crooked way to mislead it, as with the Yom Kippur goat.
וכמו שהוא הוי ערום ואזיל בעקימו הכי בעינן לאזלא בעקימו עמיה בגין למטעייה דלא יתקרב לקדושה

**Zohar I 143a** (Zohar, Toldot 19:143, expounding Psalms 120:2) — לָשׁוֹן רְמִיָּה, דְרָמֵי לֵיהּ לְאָדָם וּלְאִתְּתֵיהּ, וְאַיְיתֵי בִּישָׁא עֲלֵיהּ וְעַל עַלְמָא. לְבָתַר אֲתָא יַעֲקֹב, וְנָטִיל מִדִּילֵיהּ כָּל אִינוּן בִּרְכָאן. The "deceitful tongue" is the serpent that cast down Adam and Eve; Jacob came afterward and took from it all those blessings.
*Mafteach: found*

**Midrash Tanchuma, Toldot 1** — כָּל הַמֵּבִיא שְׁלָמִים, מֵבִיא שָׁלוֹם לָעוֹלָם... גָּדוֹל הוּא הַשָּׁלוֹם, שֶׁדִּבְּרָה הַתּוֹרָה דִּבְרֵי בְדַאי בִּשְׁבִיל שָׁלוֹם. The Tanchuma opens Toldos with peace-offerings that bring peace, then "great is peace, for the Torah recorded invented words for its sake" (Genesis 50:17). Rav Tzadok asks why peace-offerings belong here, and answers: Jacob's eating was itself a shelamim, and truth and peace are bound together.
*Mafteach: wrong address (index: תנחומא, no section given; correct: Midrash Tanchuma, Toldot 1)*

**Zohar I 142a** (Zohar, Toldot 16:126) — יַעֲקֹב כָּל עוֹבָדוֹי הֲווּ לִשְׁמָא דְקוּדְשָׁא בְּרִיךְ הוּא, וּבְגִין כָּךְ קוּדְשָׁא בְּרִיךְ הוּא הֲוָה עִמֵּיהּ תָּדִיר. All Jacob's deeds were for the sake of Heaven, so the Shechinah never left him.
*Mafteach: found*

**Proverbs 13:25** — צַדִּיק אֹכֵל לְשֹׂבַע נַפְשׁוֹ וּבֶטֶן רְשָׁעִים תֶּחְסָר. The righteous eats for his soul's satisfaction; Rav Tzadok makes Jacob's meal like an offering, a shelamim.
*Mafteach: found*

**Parallels:**
**Peri Tzadik, Toldot 5** (Rav Tzadok) — the "as we said" of this os: Zohar I 142a (all Jacob's deeds for Heaven) and צדיק אוכל לשובע נפשו make Jacob's eating "like actual offerings," so "אנכי עשו בכורך" was said truthfully, without excuses; it also explains his answer "אני." *checked*

**Zohar III 12b** (Zohar, Vayikra 25:191) — עוֹשֶׂה שָׁלוֹם בִּמְרוֹמָיו, דָּא יַעֲקֹב. דִּכְתִּיב, תִּתֵּן אֱמֶת לְיַעֲקֹב, וּכְתִיב וְהָאֱמֶת וְהַשָׁלוֹם אֱהָבוּ. דֶּאֱמֶת וְשָׁלוֹם קָשִׁיר דָּא בְּדָא. "Maker of peace" is Jacob: truth (Micah 7:20) and peace (Zechariah 8:19) are tied together. This lets the Midrash's "great is peace" belong to Jacob, the man of truth.
*Mafteach: found*

**Zohar I 138a** (Zohar, Toldot 4:26) — אָזִיל עִמֵּיהּ יַעֲקֹב בְּעֲקִימָא, כְּנָחָשׁ דְּאִיהוּ חַכִּים, וְאִיהוּ אָזִיל בְּעֲקִימוּ, כְּמָה דְאַתְּ אָמֵר, וְהַנָּחָשׁ הָיָה עָרוּם. The same Zohar as at [1.20]. Here Rav Tzadok stresses that the serpent is "wise": Jacob's crookedness is a form of wisdom (Proverbs 8:12).
*Mafteach: found*

**Genesis 27:24** — וַיֹּאמֶר אַתָּה זֶה בְּנִי עֵשָׂו וַיֹּאמֶר אָנִי. Jacob answers only "I," which Rav Tzadok explained in Toldot 5 (Rashi: he did not say "I am Esau").
*Mafteach: missing*

**Zohar I 137b** (Zohar, Toldot 4:25) — תָּא חֲזֵי, דָּא סִטְרָא דְּרוֹכֵב נָחָשׁ, וְדָא סִטְרָא דְּרוֹכֵב עַל כָּרְסְיָא שְׁלֵימָתָא קַדִּישָׁא. Esau is the side that rides the serpent; Jacob is the side that rides the complete holy throne. Mikdash Melech on Zohar 1:137b explains it the same way (Esau = Samael, Jacob = Ze'ir Anpin).
*Mafteach: wrong address (index: Zohar I 135b; correct: Zohar I 137b)*

**Ecclesiastes 7:14** — גַּם אֶת־זֶה לְעֻמַּת־זֶה עָשָׂה הָאֱלֹהִים. God made the one opposite the other; Jacob and Esau are holiness and its exact counterpart.
*Mafteach: missing*

**Malachi 1:2** — הֲלוֹא־אָח עֵשָׂו לְיַעֲקֹב נְאֻם־יְהֹוָה וָאֹהַב אֶת־יַעֲקֹב. They are brothers, matched pairs, and the same chapter then sets the "border of wickedness" against the "border of Israel."
*Mafteach: found*

**Rashi on Pesachim 54b**, s.v. מלכות חייבת — רומי שכתוב בה גבול רשעה ורשעה היינו חייבת. The Gemara lists among the seven hidden things "when the guilty kingdom will end"; Rashi identifies it as Rome, called "the border of wickedness." Rav Tzadok quotes it as "הרשעה"; the Vilna text of Gemara and Rashi reads "חייבת."
*Mafteach: found*

**Malachi 1:4–5** — וְקָרְאוּ לָהֶם גְּבוּל רִשְׁעָה... וְאַתֶּם תֹּאמְרוּ יִגְדַּל יְהֹוָה מֵעַל לִגְבוּל יִשְׂרָאֵל. Edom is "the border of wickedness"; the next verse sets against it "the border of Israel." Rav Tzadok reads the two "borders" as Malchus of holiness (Knesses Yisrael) and the kingdom of wickedness.
*Mafteach: missing*

**Tikkunei Zohar 17a** (Patach Eliyahu) — כֶּתֶר עִלְיוֹן אִיהוּ כֶּתֶר מַלְכוּת, וַעֲלֵיהּ אִתְּמַר מַגִּיד מֵרֵאשִׁית אַחֲרִית. The highest crown is the crown of Malchus: the beginning declares the end. Rav Tzadok takes it unattributed and applies it to the kelipah in reverse.
*Mafteach: missing*

**Exodus 26:28** — וְהַבְּרִיחַ הַתִּיכֹן בְּתוֹךְ הַקְּרָשִׁים מַבְרִחַ מִן־הַקָּצֶה אֶל־הַקָּצֶה; the Zohar reads it as Jacob (Zohar, Terumah 94:909: מַבְרִיחַ מִן הַקָּצֶה אֶל הַקָּצֶה, דָּא הוּא יַעֲקֹב קַדִּישָׁא שְׁלֵימָא... דְּאָחִיד לְהַאי וְאָחִיד לְהַאי). Jacob is the middle bar that holds both ends, from Keter to Malchus. The Mafteach files this under Zohar II 166b; in Sefaria's page division the passage stands on II 174b.
*Mafteach: missing*

**Numbers 24:20** — רֵאשִׁית גּוֹיִם עֲמָלֵק וְאַחֲרִיתוֹ עֲדֵי אֹבֵד. Amalek, Esau's grandson, is the "beginning" of the kelipah, the reverse of Keter in holiness.
*Mafteach: found*

**Bereshit Rabbah 63:8** — וַיִּקְרְאוּ שְׁמוֹ עֵשָׂו, הֵא שָׁוְא שֶׁבָּרָאתִי בְּעוֹלָמִי. The name Esau is read as shav, "the falsehood I created in My world." Esau is the root of falsehood, so against him truth must use stratagem.
*Mafteach: found*

**Parallels:**
**Peri Tzadik, Vayetzei 1** (Rav Tzadok) — the same pairing: Esau took this world of falsehood (Bereshit Rabbah 63, "הא שוא שבראתי בעולמי"), Jacob the world of truth (תתן אמת ליעקב). There Rav Tzadok adds that the serpent brought death through the lying lip, that Jacob said "הצילה נפשי משפת שקר" as he went in to his father (Zohar I 143a), and that "בא אחיך במרמה – בחכמת תורתו" proves he took blessings that truly were his. *checked*

**Parallels:**
**Peri Tzadik, Sukkot 12:2** (Rav Tzadok) — Jacob's dealings with Esau and Laban (the birthright, the blessings, the rods) looked like trickery but hid higher matters; "מה שהלך עם עשו ברמאות הי' לקיים בזה עם עקש תתפתל," because Esau was the full opposite of holiness (זה לעומת זה). It adds that Jacob's attribute of truth was openly confirmed only when he parted from Laban. *checked*

**Parallels beyond the library:**
**Sulam on Zohar, Toldot 194** (Kabbalah) — Jacob, "dwelling in tents" and joined to both sides, came to Esau from Isaac's side and outwitted him by the verse "with the crooked You deal subtly," receiving the blessings supported from above.
והערים עליו, כמו שלמדנו, שכתוב עם חסיד תתחסד, ועם עקש תתפל.

notes.anchor: הַצִּילָה נַפְשִׁי מִשְּׂפַת שָׁקֶר מִלָּשׁוֹן רְמִיָּה
notes.text:
**Psalms 120:2** — יְהֹוָה הַצִּילָה נַפְשִׁי מִשְּׂפַת־שֶׁקֶר מִלָּשׁוֹן רְמִיָּה. The Zohar (I 142b–143a) puts this psalm in Jacob's mouth when he stood before Isaac; Rav Tzadok identifies the "deceitful tongue" with the serpent.
*Mafteach: found*

notes.anchor: הַצִּילָה נַפְשִׁי מִשְּׂפַת שָׁקֶר מִלָּשׁוֹן רְמִיָּה
notes.text:
**Parallels:**
**Sod Yesharim, Sukkot 57** (Ishbitz–Radzin) — cites the same Zohar (Toldot 142b): Jacob said "אל ה' בצרתה לי... הצילה נפשי משפת שקר" when Isaac asked "האתה זה בני עשו," and the "lying lip" is Esau's level, the serpent that brought curses on the world. It applies the passage to the fifteen Songs of Ascents and Simchas Beis HaShoevah. *checked*

connector.why: Esau = falsehood (BR 63), Jacob = truth (Micah 7:20), Psalms 120:2 at the blessings via Zohar I 143a, BR 67 'בחכמת תורתו'; read in full.
Read 1:1–1:3 (Tanchuma openings, Abraham and Isaac crowned through Jacob); the shared Genesis 27:19 / Psalms 120:2 are not the subject of what I read.
The 'as we said' of this os: Jacob's eating as offerings (Zohar I 142a, Prov 13:25), truthful 'אנכי עשו בכורך' and 'אני'.
Opening read (Purim mitzvot, letters of Amalek against Yaakov); the shared sources were not in the portion read, so not used.
Same Zohar: Jacob says Psalms 120:2 before Isaac; 'lying lip' = Esau and the serpent.
The ref does not resolve on Sefaria; the matching text is Ohr HaChammah on Zohar 1:138a:6, which was read and used.

candidates.why: Ref as given returns 404; the passage with דרוכב/בעקימו/תתפל is Ohr HaChammah on Zohar 1:138a:6 (R. Chaim Vital): Jacob, a 'tam', goes crookedly with the serpent per עם עקש תתפל to keep it from holiness, which is the os's core idea.
Jacob outwitted Esau by 'ועם עקש תתפל' and received the blessings from both sides, the same verse and setting.
Shares only 'מצידי'; about Jacob's humble speech versus Esau's 'יקום אבי'.
Shares only the verse; Jacob is sure of success because Isaac did not recognize him. Not about truth and stratagem.

found.ref: Degel Machaneh Ephraim, Addenda on Torah, Toldot 3
found.why: Asks how Jacob, a man of truth, said 'אנכי עשו'; answers via Onkelos בחכמה and BR 'בחכמת תורתו': Jacob is Torah.
Commentary on Rav Tzadok's Zohar I 145b: 'שכנתי ערמה דא יעקב', shrewdness as Jacob's left-side component that won the blessings.
